_comment: Registered predictions whose preconditions the harness checks before GO.
Gamma's design, and the default is the whole point: `precondition` is
`unresolved` unless someone says otherwise, and a missing field counts as
unresolved too. Silence blocks rather than passes. Any scheme that needs
someone to *declare* a dependency fails the same way the ones that failed
on 2026-07-28 did - staging by path, announcing the file, checking the
diff - because declaring is the step that gets skipped.
Resolving one is an explicit act with a name on it: set `precondition` to
`resolved`, and fill `resolvedBy` and `resolvedNote`. A false block costs
a line of typing; a false pass costs a raid.
This file cannot cover registrations that live only as prose in
FINDINGS.md. The gate counts those and says how many it did not check,
because a check that appears to cover more than it does is the failure
family this whole exercise came out of.

registrations.preconditionWas: Depends on whether item 4 also latches endToStart at the frame boundary. If it does, the alignment changes and this needs re-deriving BEFORE the raid.
registrations.resolvedNote: Not re-derived before the raid - the precondition failed, which is why this gate exists. Resolved after the fact: all three registered outcome rows fail and the answer is a fourth, the two fields moving one line apart relative to each other. 22/22 at a 0.0% coincidence baseline post-latch, 12/15 at 0.7% pre-latch.

registrations.claim: unaccounted[N] ~= endToLatch[N], same line, no subtraction and no index shift
registrations.source: FINDINGS.md, 'Registered before the next raid - the one-term form, and the old field as its control'
registrations.preconditionWas: Requires endToStart to still emit in the same build as its control. Without the field being replaced still present, a fix and a silent regression produce identical output.
registrations.resolvedBy: Gamma registered 0c9b954; Beta confirms both fields emit in build e6abe58c
registrations.resolvedNote: Two rows must both hold: endToLatch[N] vs unaccounted[N] agree to well under 1 ms, AND endToStart[N-1] vs unaccounted[N] reproduces the 0.035 ms match. The second is the control - if it fails, tonight's pairing was a property of that raid rather than of the instrument. Drop endToStart once validated, not before.

registrations.claim: PRIMARY: count of spike lines with periodMs >= 100, pooled per arm, compared with an exact conditional binomial, and the detectable effect stated up front rather than after the result. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: the count at periodMs >= 30 - it must not carry a significance test. Neither is a per-window median and neither is a t-test.
registrations.source: Gamma's power analysis, 2026-07-28, as corrected by Gamma the same evening; re-derived by Alpha before the raid
registrations.preconditionNow: The >= 30 threshold was registered as PRIMARY and is withdrawn. It is not a rare-event count: re-derived on the 2026-07-28 raid at constant cfg it runs var/mean 447x with Spearman +0.75 against window order and a 6.0x rise across the raid, because it tracks the frame-time distribution and therefore the player's position - the series steps from 19,22,13,7,1,0,6,7,4,18 to 388,635,351,412,685 at the moment the runner parked on the chosen sightline. Two consequences, both fatal: the exact conditional binomial assumes Poisson and is invalid at that dispersion, so the 'resolves a few percent' figure was optimistic by roughly 20x; and a monotonic rise across a raid confounds arm with time in an ABA, where arm 3 sits late and arm 1 early. periodMs >= 100 is near-Poisson (0.9-1.2x, rho +0.18) and its power figures stand: ~2.2 events per window, ~11 per 5-minute arm, 4.5x detectable at 80 percent. BLOCKS UNTIL the protocol alternates. The fix is the alternation pattern and not the threshold: replace B1/B2/B3 with three A-blocks and three B-blocks so a monotonic drift falls on both arms and cancels in the paired comparison, and the contrast is replicated three times within the raid instead of once. 3 minutes per arm gives 3 full windows each and 18 usable windows against the ABA design's 15, so the better design is also the cheaper one. Resolve by pointing at the installed ini. FALLBACK if the protocol is not changed: run the ABA, report >= 100 as primary with 4.5x stated in advance, and treat >= 30 as descriptive - defensible, but the raid then cannot resolve an ordinary effect.
registrations.preconditionWas: Requires (a) slicing to actually engage, which ModCompat.SuppressSlicing blocks whenever BigBrain is present and Defer to other AI mods is true, and (b) a declared primary metric with a stated detectable effect size, because the 100 ms count cannot resolve an ordinary effect at the arm lengths a person will stand still for.
registrations.partiallyResolvedBy: Beta set Defer to other AI mods = false before ModCompat latches, and deployed 4867afb emitting agents.slicing / tickedSum / liveSum; Alpha verified all three in probe-symbols --key mode and moved GO. Condition (a) is met. Condition (b) is NOT - the metric that was registered is withdrawn, so this blocks until the protocol alternates or the fallback is accepted explicitly.
registrations.resolvedNote: SUPERSEDED, KEPT BECAUSE IT IS WRONG AND WAS ACTED ON. WHY 30 AND NOT 100. >=100 ms events run 2.2 per window, so a 5-minute arm holds ~11 and can only detect a 4.5x change at 80% power - an ordinary real effect would read as 'no effect'. At >=30 ms the same raid gives ~380 per window, ~1900 per 5-minute arm, resolving a few percent. The fix is the threshold, not the arm length, because nobody stands still for the 40 minutes that >=100 ms would need to reach 1.55x. COUNT period, NOT frame: the emit gate at Telemetry.cs:966 tests periodMs alone while frameMs is passed and never tested, and since frame travels one line ahead of period a large frame can sit on a line whose period is under threshold and emit nothing - counting frame >= T off the spike stream undercounts by about a third, and 8 of 16 windows have a percentile-derived lower bound that exceeds their observed count. Re-thresholding at analysis time is what makes the corpus rule about 100/50/30 irrelevant rather than violated. ARM 2 STRADDLES A KNEE: at 23 agents and 17.1 ms frames the computed perFrame is 4 and Minimum brains per frame is 4, so slicing binds above ~30 agents and the floor binds below ~15, and Streets moves across that range within a raid. Arm 2 is therefore not one condition - stratify its windows by tickedSum/liveSum, which reads which side bound per window, rather than assuming it was sliced throughout.
